review.summary: Found eight medium and two low defects, including incomplete repairs, controls that still accept wrong implementations, and publication inconsistencies. The recorded review totals and hashes agree, the 237-test suite completed without failures with two skips, and the isolated native Codex and tmux checks reproduced their expected results. Both earlier refutations are supported. Artifact execution and mutations used disposable scratch copies; the checkout remains clean at 9e55a1036c61.

claims_checked.claim: The runner records contain nine successful jobs, 46 findings with severity counts 3/34/9, and 41 reviewer-tested findings.
claims_checked.source: Recomputed from results.json and compared with the new receipt: nine jobs, all exit 0; 46 findings; 3 high, 34 medium, 9 low; tested=true on 41.

claims_checked.claim: Recorded usage is 24.47M input tokens, 95.0% cache reads, 0.36M output and approximately 71 minutes.
claims_checked.source: Runner totals are 24,470,302 input, 23,242,624 cached input and 360,897 output tokens. Cache ratio is 94.98299%; earliest start to latest finish is 71.1167 minutes. Per-job receipt values agree.

claims_checked.claim: Verifier and disposition accounting agrees across the records.
claims_checked.source: verification.json and findings.json reproduce 23 graded findings: 17 confirmed, 4 partly, 2 refuted; 11 duplicates and 12 coordinator checks. Dispositions are 39 repaired, 2 refuted, 3 removed and 2 kept.

claims_checked.claim: The two earlier refutations are correct.
claims_checked.source: Installed Claude Code 2.1.285 source and the [hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks.md), fetched 2026-09-30, support command-hook deduplication and terminal inactivity timing. The reference says "If you define the same handler in more than one settings file, it runs once" and "each keystroke defers it". No finding reopens either refutation.

claims_checked.claim: The removed second-distro findings have no remaining write path, and the kept host-ID findings are explicit residuals.
claims_checked.source: replace_bell_group.py accepts only local; the retired-target control passes and the remote write implementation is absent. findings.json explicitly records the registered host identifier as kept and its duplicate as the same convention.

claims_checked.claim: The supplied settings-swap controls and mutants reproduce their recorded results.
claims_checked.source: Scratch execution returned 24 cases, 0 problems and 15 runs, 0 problems. The after-merge and at-backup conflict controls pass. This does not substantiate the separate false assurance about saves after backup.

claims_checked.claim: Backup mode preservation is independent of the caller's umask.
claims_checked.source: With umask 077 and a 0640 settings fixture, apply exited 0 with live mode 0640 and backup mode 0600; the expanded controls returned 24 cases, 1 problem. This comes from unchanged tools/adoption/apply_claude_settings.py write_backup behavior and is excluded from findings as outside the patch.

claims_checked.claim: A save after backup creation survives in the backup.
claims_checked.source: After-backup writer injection exited 0 while both installed settings and backup retained original-model.

claims_checked.claim: The repaired notification reader reproduces the three installed-release reports and its supplied mutant results.
claims_checked.source: Scans of installed 2.1.283, 2.1.284 and 2.1.285 each exited 0 with 17 matcher values, no unknown types and output exactly equal to the corresponding recorded JSON. Eight reader tests and all seven supplied mutants behaved as recorded.

claims_checked.claim: The reader fails closed when the spread identifier has no supported array assignment.
claims_checked.source: The property-assignment/function-parameter fixture evaluated to a real catalog containing brand_new_type, but the scanner exited 0 with catalogs_resolved=true and unknown=[]. Additional unsupported numbered-name fixtures also produced false passes.

claims_checked.claim: The repaired login-shell controls reject early exits and functions, and the bash oracle checks first_read.
claims_checked.source: Nine control homes passed. The bash sweep checked 512 combinations with zero mismatches; its negative control disagreed in 26 combinations. A separate fixture showed command -v accepts a function, type -P rejects it, and exec fails with 127; a real executable passes.

claims_checked.claim: The repaired PATH digest measures the complete final PATH and distinguishes changed PATHs.
claims_checked.source: Two unmodified CLI runs returned the same startup-log digest despite different independently captured final PATHs. Newline-containing PATHs were also truncated. The supplied four selftests passed even with a constant-digest mutant.

claims_checked.claim: The repaired Codex strict-config check accepts a loaded template and rejects failures before configuration loading.
claims_checked.source: Five selftests passed, and a pre-configuration-failure shim made the script exit 1. Native codex-cli 0.159.2, with isolated HOME and CODEX_HOME and no authentication, loaded the rendered template and unknown-[tui]-key arm before expected 401 errors, rejected both negative configuration controls, and made the checker exit 0. The first isolated attempt lacked Node and was correctly rejected; adding the installed Node directory to PATH resolved that harness dependency.

claims_checked.claim: The pty probes handle a single SIGTERM and their supplied selftests pass.
claims_checked.source: Both baseline selftests passed, including their end-to-end SIGTERM cases. An independent PID-based stand-in harness confirmed that one SIGTERM removes the private directory and terminates the child.

claims_checked.claim: The pty cleanup remains effective through repeated termination signals.
claims_checked.source: Two SIGTERMs 100 ms apart left the expected sleep process in sleeping state after each parent exited 143.

claims_checked.claim: The end-to-end SIGTERM control proves that its stand-in started and was terminated.
claims_checked.source: Changing the launched executable to /bin/true left both complete selftests passing their end-to-end signal cases.

claims_checked.claim: tmux bell and synchronized-output results reproduce.
claims_checked.source: Private tmux 3.4 runs returned bell counts 1,1,0,0,0 and successful verdicts. The synchronized-output probe returned three opening/closing mode-2026 pairs with xterm*:sync and zero without. The bell selftest also passed all eight checks.

claims_checked.claim: The recorded corrected colour counts agree with the older receipt.
claims_checked.source: recorded/color_capture.txt agrees with terminal-experience-20260928.json: unset foreground/background truecolor counts 0/0 and indexed counts 37/4; truecolor-enabled counts 39/6 and indexed counts 0/0. All eight supplied counter selftests pass.

claims_checked.claim: The new colour parser correctly handles colon subparameters.
claims_checked.source: Valid and invalid colon fixtures disagree with the pinned [Windows Terminal v1.24.11911.0 parser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/terminal/v1.24.11911.0/src/terminal/adapter/adaptDispatchGraphics.cpp). The recorded semicolon-form capture counts are not disputed.

claims_checked.source: Changing Notifications' Default from true to false still returned identical=true. Multiline serde-attribute changes and significant whitespace changes inside Display strings also compared equal. All eleven supplied selftests passed. The omitted Default block exists in the tagged upstream source.

claims_checked.claim: The five affected unit-test modules run 237 tests without failures.
claims_checked.source: An isolated scratch run completed 237 tests with zero failures, zero errors and two skips. One skip is the intentionally unavailable installed-Claude test in the synthetic HOME; the other is the existing no-differing-profile case. Overlay oracle unit tests use synthetic settings; the live-overlay check was not run.

claims_checked.claim: The repaired profile-precedence and focused-tab timer statements match primary sources.
claims_checked.source: Tagged [CascadiaSettingsSerialization.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/terminal/v1.24.11911.0/src/cascadia/TerminalSettingsModel/CascadiaSettingsSerialization.cpp) calls "profile->AddMostImportantParent(userSettings.baseLayerProfile);"; [IInheritable.h](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/terminal/v1.24.11911.0/src/cascadia/TerminalSettingsModel/IInheritable.h) checks own values before parents. Tagged [Tab.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/terminal/v1.24.11911.0/src/cascadia/TerminalApp/Tab.cpp) sets the focused-tab bell timer to "std::chrono::milliseconds(2000)". Sources fetched 2026-09-30.

claims_checked.claim: The revised PushNotification presence rule is qualified to local sessions.
claims_checked.source: Installed Claude Code 2.1.285 source guards both agentPushNotifEnabled and presence checks with the non-remote condition. Presence uses focus information when available and otherwise the 60000 ms interaction threshold, matching the revised documents.

claims_checked.claim: Published receipt hashes and manifest metadata match the changed files.
claims_checked.source: Verified seven script hashes, four record hashes, 27 recorded-output hashes, eleven internally consistent prompt hashes, and SHA-256/byte-size metadata for all 71 changed files represented in manifests/evidence.json.

claims_checked.claim: The private-label repair and gateway-point figure are consistent across the new publication.
claims_checked.source: Private project labels remain in new recorded commit subjects and review JSON. The artifact README says three pool points while the receipt records [7,11] and says four.

claims_checked.source: No real interactive Claude session was run. The recorded numbers were compared, but a permitted isolated native capture or retained raw capture would be needed to establish the historical execution itself.

claims_checked.claim: The user's live overlay, live Windows Terminal sound/focus behavior and remote notification delivery satisfy the documented results.
claims_checked.source: Live settings and interactive terminal/client checks were excluded. Source review and synthetic tests establish narrower properties only. Authorized live-setting observation and terminal/remote-session measurements would settle these claims.

claims_checked.source: Its private checkout was not accessed. The copied login-shell function was tested, but validating the deployed doctor and 29-case profile checker requires their pinned source and a permitted fixture run.

findings.claim: The new backup comparison misses an atomic save made during the backup and overwrites that save without retaining a recovery copy.
findings.evidence: In ctx_execute, rtk python3 -B atomic_writer_during_backup.py interposed on acs.shutil.copyfileobj after write_backup had opened its source. It saved model='atomic-save-during-backup' using the repository's acs.atomic_write. Output: 'source inode differs from current live: True'; tool exit 0; 'read-back equals the merged copy: True'; 'FINAL LIVE MODEL original'; 'BACKUP MODELS [original]'; 'ANY RECOVERY COPY HAS NEW SAVE False'. Changing only the scratch concurrent_writer_harness.py to inject this interleaving made the existing controls report: 'the other writer’s save was lost ... the backup does not hold the newer content'; '24 cases, 1 problems'.
findings.failure_scenario: Another writer atomically replaces settings.json after write_backup opens the original inode but before it copies that inode. The backup still equals original, so the second comparison passes even though the live pathname contains newer settings. This happens before the second comparison, rather than in the acknowledged comparison-to-replace gap. The tool restores its stale model value and its backup also contains the stale value.
findings.fix: After making the backup, compare the current live file with original again and refuse if either the live file or backup differs. Add a control that atomically replaces the live pathname after the backup source is opened. Correct line 14's claim that the backup necessarily holds an intervening save, and distinguish the remaining final comparison-to-replace limitation from the protection actually tested.

findings.claim: The new signal handler can still leave the client running because the process cleanup guard starts after the client is spawned.
findings.evidence: A scratch rtk python3 -B stdin harness used a stand-in claude and a line trace to deliver the signal at os.close(slave), immediately after Popen returned. alert_probe.py: SIGTERM exit 143 and SIGHUP exit 129, both with 'private directory exists False child still running True'. The same experiment at push_notification_probe.py:297 produced the same results. The client process-group cleanup try/finally begins later in measure().
findings.failure_scenario: SIGTERM or SIGHUP arrives after the client process is created but before measure enters its observation-loop try/finally. SystemExit reaches with_private_dir and removes the payload directory, but never executes the client process-group cleanup.
findings.fix: Establish the resource cleanup guard before creating the pty and client, track which resources have been created, and protect process creation and registration from interruption. Add a signal case at this initialization boundary to both probes.

findings.claim: Restoring the original signal handlers before deleting the private directory leaves raw payloads behind when termination arrives during cleanup.
findings.evidence: Lines 263–264 restore each previous handler before shutil.rmtree(private). A scratch runner interposed on rmtree and sent SIGTERM at its entry, after work returned normally. Both alert_probe.py and push_notification_probe.py exited 143 with 'private directories left 1 payload retained True'. The corresponding restoration occurs at push_notification_probe.py:256.
findings.failure_scenario: A single SIGTERM arrives while the probe is beginning its final directory deletion. The original default handler has already been restored, so the process terminates without removing events.log. A repeated signal can similarly interrupt cleanup already triggered by an earlier signal.
findings.fix: Protect resource cleanup from SIGTERM and SIGHUP, for example by blocking or deferring them during cleanup, and restore previous handlers only after cleanup completes. Simply moving restoration below rmtree is insufficient if the raising handler can still interrupt rmtree. Add a cleanup-phase signal test.

findings.claim: The end-to-end SIGTERM check can pass without starting or terminating a stand-in client, and its process scan can mistake an unrelated process for that client.
findings.evidence: In scratch copies, measure() was changed to sleep 0.6 seconds and raise RuntimeError before spawning the client. Running the complete --selftest still returned exit 0: alert_probe had 38 PASS lines and push_notification_probe had 33 PASS lines, both ending 'PASS SIGTERM end to end: probe started True, private directory left False, stand-in client still alive False'. Separately, an unrelated Python process with an argument containing the constructed unique string made the unmodified signal_case fail with 'stand-in client still alive True', although its own stand-in had terminated.
findings.failure_scenario: The private directory appears, the probe crashes and cleans it up, and send_signal is called after the probe has already exited. Directory existence is treated as proof that the client started, so the check passes vacuously. Conversely, the substring search over every /proc cmdline can fail because of an unrelated process.
findings.fix: Have the stand-in publish its PID and a readiness marker. Require both probe and stand-in to be alive immediately before signaling, assert the probe's expected termination status, and check the recorded stand-in PID or process group instead of searching unrelated command lines. Apply the same correction to alert_probe.py.

findings.claim: The derived probe's hooks-disabled control still exits successfully after observing a forbidden BEL.
findings.evidence: With a synthetic HOME and stand-in claude that printed 'Enter to select' and emitted one BEL nine seconds after startup, rtk python3 -B push_notification_probe.py ask --control printed 'dialog_opened=True' and 'bare BEL bytes after the dialog opened: 1', then exited 0. The identical input to alert_probe.py exited 1 with 'a hooks-disabled control saw a BEL byte'. Both quiet controls exited 0.
findings.failure_scenario: A caller uses the supported ask --control mode of push_notification_probe.py and checks only its exit status. A BEL appears while every hook is disabled, invalidating attribution to the notification hook, but the caller receives success.
findings.fix: Apply the repaired alert_probe exit-status logic to the derived probe: return 1 when a hooks-disabled control observes a post-dialog BEL and retain 2 when the observation point is never reached. Add the corresponding exit-status cases and a stand-in CLI test.

findings.claim: The new assertion that a 0640 backup preserves its mode is not valid under a restrictive umask.
findings.evidence: Running rtk python3 -B replace_bell_group_controls.py D with subprocess umask 077 returned exit 1: 'WRONG --apply keeps a file mode other than 0600 on the installed file and on its backup ... the backup does not keep the mode'; '24 cases, 1 problems'. A direct synthetic-home run exited 0 with installed mode 0640 and backup mode 0600. write_backup creates the backup with os.open and does not subsequently restore its mode. Python's documentation states: 'When computing mode, the current umask value is first masked out.' [Python os.open documentation](https://docs.python.org/3.11/library/os.html#os.open), fetched 2026-09-30.
findings.failure_scenario: A user runs the controls or replacement tool from a shell with umask 077 against a 0640 settings file. The new control fails, and the README's claim that the backup keeps that mode is false.
findings.fix: If exact backup-mode preservation is the intended contract, explicitly restore the source mode on the opened backup and add a umask-077 case. Otherwise, change the assertion and documentation to describe the backup's umask-filtered permissions rather than exact preservation.

findings.claim: The repaired reader can still select an unrelated scope's array and successfully omit an unknown notification type.
findings.evidence: In a scratch copy, `rtk python3 -B notification_types_scan.py <other-scope-nested-assignment> <checkout>` returned exit 0, `catalogs_resolved: true`, `base_candidates: 1`, and `unknown: []`. The fixture has an unrelated function assigning Ojo=["permission_prompt","idle_prompt"] and the catalog's function assigning Ojo=[...Q,"brand_new_type"]. `rtk node -e <same fixture>` returned ["permission_prompt","idle_prompt","brand_new_type","elicitation_complete","elicitation_response"]. A second fixture containing one recognized catalog and another with values:[...(true?Q:Ojo),"elicitation_response"] also returned exit 0 while omitting the second catalog.

The global literal-assignment search finds only the unrelated assignment, calls the catalog resolved, and approves a bundle containing an unclassified type. An unsupported additional catalog is likewise invisible when another catalog matches the regex.
findings.fix: Account for every notification_type catalog marker and fail closed on unsupported catalog expressions. Resolve spread identifiers within their lexical scope, or refuse resolution when another assignment cannot be accounted for. Add the scoped nested-assignment and mixed recognized/unrecognized catalog fixtures; each must either report brand_new_type as UNKNOWN or exit nonzero as unresolved.

findings.claim: The new PATH protocol mistakes startup output for the measurement and can report identical digests for different final PATH values.
findings.evidence: Ran the CLI against temporary homes whose startup file first executes `printf "PATH=%s\n" "$PATH"`, then prepends either $HOME/binA or $HOME/binB. Both runs exited 0 and reported 9 entries with digest f5a00065660f4ba1. An independent final-PATH probe using the identical HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL and distro-default PATH environment observed 10 entries, with different digests 238582c9668d92cc and d01e10b73ff91e94. A startup `echo welcome` instead caused exit 1 with `the login shell ended before the PATH probe completed`, although that probe completed. The same first-line parsing in scrub_placeholder_probe.py returned None for welcome output and 'bogus' for an earlier PATH=bogus line.
findings.failure_scenario: A healthy login startup file prints a welcome message or logs PATH before modifying it. Ordinary output produces a false measurement error; an earlier PATH= line produces a successful measurement of the wrong value, hiding an actual PATH change.
findings.fix: Separate probe output from startup stdout using a dedicated descriptor or pipe, or read an unambiguous final adjacent PATH/DONE record instead of lines[0]. Apply the repair to scrub_placeholder_probe.py's login_path too. Add controls with startup logging and two different final PATH values, asserting the actual counts and hashes.

findings.claim: Flattening semicolon parameters and colon subparameters misclassifies valid truecolor sequences as basic colors.
findings.evidence: A scratch Python harness calling sgr_counts('ESC[38:2::31:32:33m') returned fg_truecolor_38;2=0 and basic_16=1; sgr_counts('ESC[38:2::1:2:3m') counted no color. The empty slot is the color-space slot. The pinned Windows Terminal dispatch reads RGB after it, including `const size_t red = options.at(2).value_or(0);`, and applies the color when that slot is empty. Source: [microsoft/terminal v1.24.11911.0 adaptDispatchGraphics.cpp](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/terminal/v1.24.11911.0/src/terminal/adapter/adaptDispatchGraphics.cpp), fetched 2026-09-30.
findings.failure_scenario: A capture contains the colon-form truecolor sequence ESC[38:2::31:32:33m. The terminal sets RGB(31,32,33), but the measurement reports a basic-color sequence. Similar empty-component inputs cause RGB channel values to be reinterpreted as independent SGR options.
findings.fix: Preserve colon subparameter groups when splitting semicolon parameters. Handle the empty color-space slot and component defaults according to the pinned dispatch, and consume the entire extended-color group so RGB channels cannot become basic-color options. Add these cases to the selftest with expectations derived from the upstream parser.

findings.claim: The supposedly whole-definition comparison silently excludes multiline attributes and can report identical notification definitions after their serialized names change.
findings.evidence: In a scratch harness, reformatted SYNTHETIC's serde attributes as `#[serde(\n    rename_all = "lowercase"\n)]`, then changed the first rename_all value to "UPPERCASE". definitions_identical(old,new) returned True. The prefix pattern only accepts attributes without a newline. A mutant replacing the entire prefix with an empty regex also passed `rtk python3 -B <mutant> --selftest`: exit 0, 11 checks, no problems.
findings.failure_scenario: Upstream formats a serde attribute across multiple lines and later changes its rename_all rule. Although notification setting spellings change, the refresh reports notification_definitions_identical=true because the attribute was omitted from both extracted declarations.
findings.fix: Capture complete multiline attribute blocks attached to each declaration, and return unknown when extraction cannot account for them. Add a changed multiline serde attribute control and a mutant that drops declaration attributes; both must be detected.

findings.claim: The append and replacement selftests can pass without observing either file because they compare against an already-dirty baseline.
findings.evidence: Mutated real_home_state to skip .profile and .zshrc after lstat. `rtk python3 -B <mutant> --selftest` still exited 0 with all ten results true, including appending_detected and replacing_a_file_with_a_same_size_copy_detected. A separate fresh-state harness showed the mutant missed both operations: `omission mutant append missed True` and `omission mutant replacement missed True`. Before those selftest checks, .bashrc's mtime has already been moved five seconds away from base.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression stops tracking .profile or .zshrc. The claimed controls still pass because the earlier .bashrc modification makes every later whole-state comparison unequal, regardless of whether the current operation was detected.
findings.fix: Use a fresh home or a fresh immediately-before snapshot for each operation. Assert that the specific changed entry differs and unrelated entries remain equal. Isolate inode detection by preserving size, mode and mtime during replacement, and require omission and dropped-inode mutants to fail.

findings.claim: The repaired documentation control still accepts a wrong operative matcher beside a correct historical quote when the wrong matcher omits permission_prompt.
findings.evidence: In a scratch checkout, changed the operative matcher in both the recipe and decision record to `worker_permission_prompt|push_notification`, then appended the correct overlay matcher as a historical backtick quote. `rtk python3 -B -m unittest tests.test_windows_terminal_defaults.DocumentationTests` returned exit 0: Ran 3 tests, OK. quoted_matchers filters out every list that does not contain permission_prompt, so only the correct historical quote reaches the comparison.

Add controls for a wrong active list missing permission_prompt and a single-type matcher beside a correct historical quote.

findings.claim: The repaired login check still reports success for commands that the profile's exec cannot start: type -P can return a stale hashed pathname.
findings.evidence: In a scratch home, .bash_profile populated Bash's command hash with nonexistent paths for claude, codex, nativestack and rtk. A python3 -B harness called login_shell_check(home) and returned {'pass': True, 'missing_in_login_shell': [], 'probe_completed': True, 'exit': 0}. In the same home, type -P claude printed the nonexistent pathname, test -x failed, and exec claude exited 127 with 'No such file or directory'. The [Bash Reference Manual](https://tiswww.case.edu/php/chet/bash/bashref.html#Bash-Builtin-Commands), fetched 2026-09-30, also documents that -p and -P can print hashed values.
findings.failure_scenario: A startup file contains hash -p "$HOME/missing/claude" claude and equivalent entries for the other required commands. The doctor reports a healthy login environment even though starting the client fails with exit 127.
findings.fix: Require the resolved pathname to be a regular executable file, rather than accepting any nonempty type -P output. Add a synthetic home with stale hashed paths and require it to fail. Qualify the recipe and platform statements that type -P finds files only.

findings.claim: The new protocol hashes the first PATH= line, which can come from startup output instead of the completed probe.
findings.evidence: A scratch-home python3 -B harness used .profile containing printf "PATH=%s\n" "$PATH" followed by an export of the final PATH. For final values /first/bin:/usr/bin:/bin and /second/bin:/usr/bin:/bin, independent Bash probes printed those different values, but measure(home) returned the identical accepted result in both arms: login_path_entries=9 and login_path_sha256_prefix=f5a00065660f4ba1, with no measurement_error. The same harness showed scrub_placeholder_probe.login_path(home) returning the earlier startup PATH in both arms.
findings.failure_scenario: A startup file prints a PATH diagnostic before changing PATH. Changing the final login PATH leaves the reported digest unchanged, falsely supporting the documented conclusion that the change altered nothing.
findings.fix: Parse the PATH record immediately preceding the final DONE marker, or use a separate output channel for the probe protocol. Apply the correction to scrub_placeholder_probe.login_path as well. Add a case with startup PATH diagnostics and assert the exact final value and digest.

findings.claim: The new append and replacement controls remain green for broken implementations because earlier mutations permanently changed the shared baseline.
findings.evidence: In scratch copies, a python3 -B harness removed .profile from REAL_HOME_NAMES and separately removed inode from the recorded metadata tuple. Both mutants' --selftest runs exited 0 with all_detected_as_expected=true, including appending_detected and replacing_a_file_with_a_same_size_copy_detected. An isolated same-size, same-mode, same-mtime replacement changed the inode but compared unchanged under the inode-blind mutant. Lines 107-114 compare subsequent mutations with the original baseline after .bashrc's mtime has already changed.

findings.fix: Give each mutation a fresh home or a fresh baseline taken immediately before that mutation. Assert that the intended file's entry changed. Preserve size, mode and mtime in the replacement case so that removing inode comparison makes that case fail.

findings.claim: The repaired comparison still reports identical notification definitions when a multiline serde attribute changes their configuration semantics.
findings.evidence: A scratch-copy python3 -B harness formatted NotificationMethod's attribute as #[serde(\n    rename_all = "lowercase"\n)] and compared it with the same definition using "UPPERCASE". definitions_identical(old, new) returned True; the extracted NotificationMethod contained no rename_all attribute. The equivalent single-line change returned False. [Serde's container-attribute documentation](https://serde.rs/container-attrs.html), fetched 2026-09-30, confirms that rename_all changes serialized and deserialized enum variant names.

findings.fix: Include complete preceding multiline attribute blocks in the extracted item, and return unknown when attributes cannot be captured reliably. Add a multiline lowercase-to-UPPERCASE fixture that must return False.

findings.claim: The decision record presents the strengthened real-home isolation measurement as a recorded native rerun, but the referenced receipt retains only its synthetic selftest.
findings.evidence: Line 225 states that 19 real-home names 'were unchanged by lstat mode, size, mtime and inode' and that 'a rerun with the revised script is recorded in the 2026-09-30 receipt'. Inspecting the new receipt and recorded outputs found only scrub_placeholder_probe_selftest.txt; recorded/exit_codes.txt:16 says 'exit 0 <- python3 -B scrub_placeholder_probe.py --selftest'. findings.fix: Keep the historical row scoped to its original existence comparison and describe the stronger checker as a synthetic validation. Alternatively, retain the actual revised native-run summary, including its 19-name metadata fields, and register its command and hash in the new receipt.

findings.claim: The new probe's temporary-directory-only claim is false: -L creates a socket outside its private directory and the socket survives successful cleanup.
findings.evidence: A scratch-copy python3 -B harness ran the unchanged probe with TMUX_TMPDIR pointing to a separate scratch socket directory. findings.claim: The new assurance that the backup preserves a save made between backup and replacement is false.
findings.evidence: The changed text says: "change in the last instant between the backup and the replace is not excluded (the backup then holds it)." In a scratch HOME, a python3 -B runpy harness wrapped acs.atomic_write to change model to changed-after-backup immediately before the real replacement. The unmodified tool exited 0 and printed "read-back equals the merged copy: True"; inspection reported "installed model original-model" and "backup models ['original-model']".

Explicitly state that it can be absent from both the installed file and backup, and qualify the decision record's statement that the tool installs only over the bytes it read. Add an after-backup injection case to keep the documented residual accurate.

findings.claim: The repaired digest can successfully hash startup logging instead of the final PATH, making different PATHs compare equal.
findings.evidence: A scratch .bash_profile printed "PATH=logged-before-final-path\n", then assigned PATH="/synthetic/first:$PATH"; a second run used /synthetic/second. Both unmodified CLI runs exited 0 with login_path_entries=1 and login_path_sha256_prefix=2872b9f4cd092719. Independent NUL-framed captures using the same HOME, USER, LOGNAME, SHELL and distro default PATH measured 10 entries and different digests: 2755fd727acd8653 and 36fd9d2c29da5499. The code validates the final DONE but hashes lines[0].

findings.fix: Use an unambiguous, binary-safe final PATH record and hash its complete payload; reject malformed framing. Add tests asserting exact entry counts and digests for startup output and newline-containing paths, rather than merely checking that a digest exists.

findings.claim: A second termination signal interrupts cleanup and leaves the client running.
findings.evidence: A python3 -B scratch harness ran each unmodified probe against a synthetic claude that recorded its PID and exec'd /bin/sleep 300. One SIGTERM produced exit 143 with the child gone. Two SIGTERMs 100 ms apart produced exit 143 with the child remaining. A follow-up check confirmed State: S (sleeping) and the expected sleep command, excluding a zombie-process false positive. This reproduced in alert_probe.py and push_notification_probe.py, whose corresponding handler is at line 249. Both reported their raw payload directory removed. verification.json explicitly required: "A repeated signal during cleanup should be ignored."
findings.failure_scenario: The first SIGTERM enters measure's finally block. A second SIGTERM during its cleanup sleeps raises another SystemExit, bypassing process-group termination. The parent exits while its client continues running.
findings.fix: Ignore further SIGTERM and SIGHUP signals once shutdown begins, through both child-process and private-directory cleanup. Restore previous handlers only after cleanup completes. Add a two-signal test that verifies the child was running before interruption and is gone afterward.

findings.claim: The new end-to-end SIGTERM control passes even when its stand-in client never starts.
findings.evidence: In scratch copies, replacing only subprocess.Popen(["claude", "--model" with subprocess.Popen(["/bin/true", "--model" left both complete --selftest runs exiting 0. Each printed: "PASS SIGTERM end to end: probe started True, private directory left False, stand-in client still alive False". The started predicate only checks whether an alert-probe-* directory exists. The same defect is at push_notification_probe.py:128.
findings.failure_scenario: A broken launcher creates the probe directory but never executes the stand-in. The test interprets directory creation as startup and absence of the never-created child as successful cleanup.
findings.fix: Have the stand-in publish a PID/readiness token, require that exact process to be alive before sending SIGTERM, and verify its termination afterward. Add the never-started-client mutant and require the control to reject it.

findings.claim: The repaired resolver accepts an unrelated property assignment as the catalog's identifier assignment and can silently miss an unknown notification type.
findings.evidence: The scratch fixture assigned obj.Ojo=["permission_prompt","idle_prompt"], defined f(Ojo) returning a catalog with values:[...Ojo,"elicitation_complete","elicitation_response"], and called f with an additional brand_new_type. Node evaluated the actual catalog as five types including brand_new_type. Running python3 -B notification_types_scan.py against the same file exited 0 with catalogs_resolved=True, unknown=[], and matcher_values=4. The pattern (?<![\w$]) permits the dot before obj.Ojo, although the catalog spreads a function parameter with no supported array assignment.
findings.failure_scenario: A client bundle contains a parameterized catalog and an unrelated property with the same short name. The reader reports successful resolution using the property's array and misses a type in the real catalog, instead of failing closed.
findings.fix: Exclude member access from the assignment boundary, for example by changing the negative lookbehind to (?<![\w$.]). Add this complete fixture expecting zero base candidates, unresolved catalog status and a nonzero CLI exit; add a mutant that removes the dot exclusion.

findings.claim: The notification-definition comparison still omits Notifications' Default implementation and reports identical definitions when notifications change from enabled to disabled by default.
findings.evidence: A scratch python3 -B harness compared SYNTHETIC plus an impl Default for Notifications returning Self::Enabled(true) with the same text returning Self::Enabled(false). Output: "landscape default true-to-false identical True captured parts 6". All eleven supplied selftests also passed. The tagged [Codex types.rs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openai/codex/rust-v0.157.1/codex-rs/config/src/types.rs), fetched 2026-09-30, contains "impl Default for Notifications" returning "Self::Enabled(true)". The earlier verifier's F-sol-u498-A-6 repair explicitly required the Default implementation.
findings.failure_scenario: An upstream release changes only the Notifications default. The refresh reports notification_definitions_identical=true despite a behavior change that the agreed repair was supposed to detect.
findings.fix: Include the complete Notifications Default implementation among the required comparison blocks. Return null when it is missing, and add controls for both a changed implementation and a missing implementation.

findings.claim: Flattening colon subparameters into semicolon parameters misclassifies valid truecolor and makes the new colon selftest assert the wrong result.
findings.evidence: Calling sgr_counts on ESC[38:2::31:32:33m returned fg_truecolor_38;2=0 and basic_16=1. ESC[38:2:1:2:3m returned fg_truecolor_38;2=1, and all eight selftests passed. The pinned [Windows Terminal parser](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/microsoft/terminal/v1.24.11911.0/src/terminal/adapter/adaptDispatchGraphics.cpp), fetched 2026-09-30, uses "const bool hasColorSpaceId = options.at(1).has_value();" and applies colon RGB only with an empty color-space field. RGB occupies subsequent subparameters. Thus the first tested sequence is valid and the selftest's second sequence is rejected by the pinned terminal.
findings.failure_scenario: Valid colon RGB containing the empty color-space field is rejected by the counter, which then counts RGB components such as 31, 32 and 33 as basic colors. Conversely, the new selftest blesses an invalid nonempty color-space identifier.
findings.fix: Keep semicolon parameters and colon subparameter groups distinct. Consume each color group as a unit and follow the pinned parser's color-space, component and default rules. Replace the invalid fixture and add a valid colon fixture with RGB values overlapping basic-color codes.

findings.claim: The append and replacement controls cannot establish that those changes are detected because an earlier fixture change already makes the comparison unequal.
findings.evidence: The selftest changes .bashrc's mtime at line 107 and leaves it different from base before testing .profile appending and .zshrc replacement. In a scratch mutation, real_home_state was changed to skip .profile and .zshrc entirely. Both the original and mutated --selftest exited 0, reporting appending_detected=true, replacing_a_file_with_a_same_size_copy_detected=true and all_detected_as_expected=true.
findings.failure_scenario: A regression stops observing the appended or replaced files. These controls still pass because the earlier .bashrc difference satisfies real_home_state(root) != base independently of the operation being tested.
findings.fix: Give each mutation an independent fixture or a fresh baseline immediately before that operation. Add mutants omitting the relevant observations and require the corresponding controls to fail.

findings.claim: The privacy repair removes private project labels from the older receipt but republishes them in the new review artifacts.
findings.evidence: The numbered file read shows: "636e7ea README: the second distro (Polaris) was unregistered on 2026-09-29; <project> runs in NativeStack, <project> is archived". A scoped rg search also finds the private labels in results.json:577,2040,2092 and verification.json:68,70. findings.json marks F-sol-u498-B-4 repaired; only the registered host identifier was explicitly kept.
findings.failure_scenario: Publishing the new artifact directory exposes the labels removed by the privacy repair and additionally publishes their operational status.
findings.fix: Replace the private labels with generic placeholders throughout the new review JSON and recorded commit subjects. Extend the publishing sanitizers and regenerate affected hashes and manifest entries.

findings.claim: The README reports three gateway-pool points while the receipt and decision record report four.
findings.evidence: README.md:17-18 says "71 minutes of wall clock; three points of the gateway pool's hundred used." The receipt records gateway_pool_points_used_before_and_after=[7,11], and its claim and the decision record say four. JSON arithmetic confirms a difference of 4.
findings.failure_scenario: Readers get conflicting consumption figures for the same review depending on which new record they consult.
findings.fix: Change the README to four points and retain the receipt's qualification that these are cached aggregate before/after figures that may include other sessions.
